finding: New `else if !canon.is_file()` (plus the empty-path filter at 1146/1103) makes `validate_for_install` REJECT states that previously validated green. Because `validate_for_install` is re-run on EVERY launch (runner.rs:1248 spawn_run, runner.rs:1552 resume_run), this is a behaviour regression for already-installed workflows, and it is silent for one class the diff never considers: a MOCKED step. runner.rs:758-768 short-circuits a step with `mock:` (or `force_mocks`) through `run_mock_step` BEFORE any dispatcher runs, so the prompt_file is never read. State that exposes it: a dev workflow (`is_dev=true`) with `- id: s, kind: llm, mock: {...}, prompt_file: "prompts/"` (a directory) or `prompt_file: ""`. Before: installed, launched, mock served, run SUCCEEDED. After: spawn_run returns 400 WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING / WORKFLOW_PROMPT_MISSING and no run row is created at all. Same shape for a non-mocked broken step late in the DAG: previously the run started and earlier steps' outputs/artifacts were persisted before the step failed; now nothing runs and the failure surfaces as a launch-endpoint 400 instead of a failed run in history.

The docstring asserts INV-1 in BOTH directions — "a definition the validator reports green cannot fail here, and one it reports red cannot quietly succeed here". The second half is false. `load_raw_prompt` does no path-shape or confinement check whatsoever: `bundle_root.join(rel)` + `read_to_string`. `load_raw_prompt("s", bundle, &None, &Some("../../etc/passwd".into()))` returns Ok(<contents of /etc/passwd>) on any box where it is world-readable, while the validator reports WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE (validate.rs:1150-1157). Same for a bundle-internal symlink that resolves outside the root: validator → WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_ESCAPE (validate.rs:1168), runner → Ok. The invariant holds only because validate_for_install happens to be called first; nothing in dispatch enforces it. TEST-1's `files` array (dispatch.rs:1961-1967) contains None / "" / real.md / adir / nope.md — i.e. it excludes exactly the two cells that falsify the property, while its doc claims it walks "the whole authorable state space". Adding Some("../../etc/passwd") to that array turns TEST-1 red today.

The new directory branch reuses code WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING, and validate.rs:1181 asserts "Reuses the existing code, so the builder's author-facing copy needs no new entry." That is wrong: the copy for that code reads "This step points at a prompt file that isn't in the workflow — add the file, or type the prompt in directly." For `prompt_file: "prompts/adir"` the file-ish thing IS in the workflow and the remedy "add the file" is both false and unactionable — the author must instead point at a FILE inside that directory. This is precisely the false-author-facing-reason class (INV-6 / the builder's own DESIGN 2.5 rule) that the rest of this branch exists to eliminate, reintroduced by the reuse. Note the diff DID mint distinct copy for UNSAFE vs ESCAPE on exactly this reasoning (validationCopy.ts:106-114), so the precedent for a new entry is already in the file.

The new comment claims the padding rewrite is "RTL-correct", but the fix only converted the ADDON's own padding to logical (`ps`/`pe`). `InputGroup` itself (input-group.tsx:17, tokens `has-[>[data-align=inline-end]]:[&>input]:pr-1.5` and `has-[>[data-align=inline-start]]:[&>input]:pl-1.5`) still compensates the INPUT with PHYSICAL padding keyed off the LOGICAL `data-align` attribute. Before this change both halves were physical, so they were consistently wrong under RTL and cancelled out; now they disagree. State that exposes it: load the gallery with `?dir=rtl` (GALLERY_DIRS supports it, `_gallery.ts:53`) and render a combobox — the addon moves to the visual left (order-last + logical padding) while the input's extra 6px of padding stays on the visual right, i.e. on the side with no addon. The change makes the RTL rendering worse, not better, and the new spec cannot see it because it only loads `/gallery.html` with no `dir` param (input-group-overflow.spec.ts:95).

The new spec settles the gallery with a fixed `page.waitForTimeout(1500)` after `domcontentloaded` (also at :146). Every gallery PAGE surface is a `React.lazy` resolved over the shared Vite dev server (sdk/packages/gallery/src/runtime/pages.tsx `LazyComponentRenderer`), and that file's own PreloadGate comment documents at length that under CONCURRENT gallery loads those HTTP responses become "delayed and JITTERY". This config is `fullyParallel: true` with `workers: undefined` (playwright.visual.config.ts:30-36), so these 3 tests race every other visual spec against one dev server. The sibling spec that only needs the surface MANIFEST already budgets 2000ms (form-label-starvation.spec.ts:41). Consequence is silent, not red: the two vacuity guards (`groups.length > 0` at :100, `addonPastEnd !== null` count at :121) are satisfied by the eagerly-rendered kit STORY sections (stories are synchronous — GalleryPage.tsx:92-96, controls.story.tsx:328 Combobox), so a run in which zero lazy page surfaces resolved still reports PASS while measuring a small fraction of the intended surface.

The docstring claims the spec asserts the property "over the whole backend-free gallery". It navigates to bare `STANDALONE_PATH` ('/gallery.html', _gallery.ts:10) with no theme/accent/dir query and never enumerates surfaces, so it measures only what the default landing render happens to contain at that instant. Two concrete gaps: (a) it never runs under `dir=rtl`, so the RTL branch of `probeGroups` (:76) is dead code that has never executed and its correctness is unverified; (b) it never runs under `theme=dark` or any non-default accent even though the assertion is nominally theme-independent. Combined with the fixed 1500ms wait this makes the claimed coverage substantially wider than the enforced coverage.

The diff rewrote the `promptSuppliedByFile` doc to the new rule but left the doc 20 lines above it — on `promptField`, in the same file the diff edits — stating the OLD rule verbatim: "MIRRORS `validate.rs` (~681-691) ... has_file = prompt_file.is_some()". That is exactly the line this change invalidated (validate.rs:1103 now filters empties), and it is the doc a reader consults for the requiredness rule. It also cites hard line numbers (~681-691) that the diff itself shifted.

The JSDoc block the diff expands ("Whether a step supplies its wording from a file...", :212-222) is orphaned: it is immediately followed by a SECOND JSDoc block for `PROMPT_FROM_FILE_NOTE` (:223-230) and then the const, so the function it describes is 24 lines further down at :236 with no doc attached. Tooling (hover, tsdoc, API extractors) attaches nothing to `promptSuppliedByFile` and stacks two doc comments on the const. Pre-existing misplacement, but the diff invested new explanatory text into a comment that no reader of the function will see.

`PromptSource::Missing | PromptSource::Both` are collapsed into one opaque message, "step '<id>' has invalid prompt config". The new code KNOWS which of the two it is (that is the whole point of the enum) and discards it. A runtime failure here now tells the operator nothing about whether the step has no prompt at all or two competing ones — and this arm is only reachable when validation was bypassed or the bundle changed under a running server, i.e. exactly the case where the distinction matters most. The validator produces two distinct codes/messages for the same two states (validate.rs:688-699); the runner should at minimum say which.

`canon.is_file()` swallows the underlying io::Error — `Path::is_file` returns false on ANY metadata failure (EACCES on a parent component after canonicalize, ELOOP, EIO), not just "is a directory". Those all get reported to the author as "prompt_file '

' is not a file in the bundle", whose builder copy then tells them to "add the file" (validationCopy.ts:104) — a remedy that cannot fix a permissions error. The surrounding code already distinguishes error kinds (the Err(_) arm at :1191); this branch should use `canon.metadata()` and keep the error text.

A pre-existing verdict DID move and nothing guards it. `prompt: "x"` + `prompt_file: ""` was WORKFLOW_PROMPT_BOTH under the old rule (has_prompt=true AND has_file=prompt_file.is_some()=true), i.e. install-blocking; under `prompt_source` it is `Inline("x")` and validates completely clean. TEST-3's explicitly-labelled "Pre-existing verdicts unmoved" block (validate.rs:1834-1845) does not contain this cell, and TEST-1 only asserts the two SIDES agree — which they do — so the flip is invisible to both new tests. Worth an explicit assertion either way, since it silently makes a previously-uninstallable definition installable.

`check_prompt_files` performs BLOCKING std::fs syscalls (`bundle_root.is_dir()` :1135, `resolved.canonicalize()` :1165, `bundle_root.canonicalize()` :1167) directly on a tokio worker thread, since `validate_for_install` is a sync fn called from the async `spawn_run`/`resume_run` (runner.rs:1248/1552) and from the async validate handlers. The diff adds one MORE stat per llm/llm_map/agent step (`canon.is_file()`). Pre-existing class (CODING_GUIDELINES §5 "No std::fs in async"), but the change extends it on the per-run hot path, where a workflow with many prompt_file steps on a slow/network mount will now block the runtime measurably longer.

Three different magnitudes are given for the SAME measurement across the one change, so no reader can tell which was actually observed: this comment says the old margin gave "each group 5px of horizontal scrollable overflow"; builder-responsive.spec.ts:81-85 says "the combobox's InputGroup inline-end addon rendered ~4px past its own group"; input-group-overflow.spec.ts:16 says "measured at 3.8px past the group". Since the parent diff also lowers MAX_TOLERATED_OVERFLOW_PX from 4 to 1 on the strength of this measurement, and JITTER_PX is 1, the discrepancy is load-bearing: if the real residual is 3.8 rounded to 4 rather than 0, the tightened threshold flips that spec red.

REJECTED: candidate was that the `agent` step kind has its own prompt resolution still matching (Option, Option) raw, which would make the `agent` third of TEST-1's matrix test a function the agent path never calls. Ruled out — agent_dispatch.rs:52 imports `resolve_prompt` from dispatch and :1101 calls it, and `resolve_prompt` (dispatch.rs:92) now delegates to the shared `load_raw_prompt`. All three kinds genuinely route through the one rule.

REJECTED: candidate was that the frontend `promptSuppliedByFile` change needs mirroring into the desktop UI workspace (the repo mirrors gallery/kit code into src-app/desktop/ui). Ruled out — src-app/desktop/ui/src/modules contains only chat/desktop-base/file-dialog/host-mount/layouts/memory/remote-access/tunnel-auth/updater/window; there is no workflow module there, so nothing to mirror.

REJECTED: candidate was that `has-[>button]:ps-1` would lose the cascade to the bare `ps-2` on the same element (the old code used margins, so the two never collided on one property; the new code puts both on padding-inline-start). Ruled out — per CSS Selectors 4, `:has()` contributes the specificity of its most specific argument, so `.has-\[\>button\]\:ps-1:has(>button)` is (0,1,1) against `.ps-2` (0,1,0) and wins regardless of emission order. tailwind-merge also treats modifier-prefixed utilities as a separate conflict group, so `cn()` does not strip either.

REJECTED: candidate was that the kit fix lands only in sdk source and the UI/gallery consumes a prebuilt dist, so the submodule bump alone would not change rendered output and both e2e specs would assert against stale CSS. Ruled out — sdk/packages/kit/package.json declares "main"/"types": "src/index.ts" and the UI depends on "@ziee/kit": "*" via the npm workspace, i.e. the source file is compiled by Vite directly. No build step is missing.

REJECTED: candidate was that moving llm_map's prompt load behind the shared rule perturbed the ordering guarantee that the RAW prompt is loaded on the main task (holding &ctx) before per-item tasks are spawned, which H4 depends on. Ruled out — the call site is unchanged in position and awaitedness; only its argument list narrowed from (&StepDef,&RunContext) to (&str,&Path). The raw string is still produced once, before the spawn loop, and moved in.

REJECTED: candidate was that the client and backend still disagree on whitespace — `promptField` applies `z.string().trim().min(1)`, so `prompt: "   "` with no prompt_file is a client-side error while `prompt_source` (validate.rs:1086) deliberately does NOT trim and calls it a valid Inline prompt. Ruled out as a finding of THIS diff: the `.trim()` predates the change (unmodified line), the divergence is in the safe direction (client stricter than server, so nothing false-green reaches the author), and stepForms.test.ts:279 already pins the client behaviour.

`load_raw_prompt` does an UNCONFINED `bundle_root.join(rel)` + `read_to_string` with no canonicalize/starts_with of its own — it borrows its entire safety from `validate::check_prompt_files` having run first. That trust is not universal: `spawn_run` (runner.rs:1248) and `resume_run` (runner.rs:1552) call `validate_for_install`, but `POST /api/workflows/{id}/test` (handlers/dev.rs:1115) only calls `parse_workflow_yaml` and never validates, and it is gated by the SAME `WorkflowsExecute` + `user_can_access` as /run. A `real_llm` fixture leaves llm/agent steps un-mocked (runner.rs:758 only short-circuits when a mock exists), so those steps reach this join with zero path checking. Concrete: on a workflow whose bundle contains `prompts/task.md`, replace that file on disk with a symlink to the server's `config/dev.yaml` (or add a bundle asset after install); `/run` and `/resume` reject it with WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_ESCAPE, `/test` reads it, sends it to the model, and writes it verbatim to the owner-readable step prompt log (`log_io::write_text_log`, dispatch.rs:172). The diff also WIDENS what reaches this join: `prompt: Some("") + prompt_file: Some(rel)` used to hit the `_ => Err` arm and now resolves to `PromptSource::File(rel)` and reads. Fix: re-run the confinement check (canonicalize + starts_with(bundle_root)) inside `load_raw_prompt`, or make `/test` call `validate_for_install` like its siblings.

TOCTOU between validation and use survives the refactor. `check_prompt_files` (validate.rs:1163-1177) canonicalizes `bundle_root.join(p)` and proves confinement at spawn/resume time; `load_raw_prompt` later re-joins the RAW relative string and reads it, with an arbitrary gap (a long-running workflow, a `waiting`/durable-resume gate) in between and no re-check. Anything with write access to `extracted_path` during that window (another server-side feature, a shared-tmp neighbour, a crashed `.staging-*`/`.old-*` swap left behind by `update_user_workflow_definition`) can swap a validated regular file for a symlink out of the bundle and the run will read it. The narrowed `(step_id, &Path)` signature introduced here was the natural place to fold the confinement in and it was not taken.

The textual shape reject `p.contains("..") || p.starts_with('/')` is the ONLY prompt_file check that runs when `bundle_present == false` (validate.rs:1158 `continue`), and this diff re-plumbed its input (`prompt_file_ref`) without widening it. It does not recognise Windows-absolute or UNC paths: `prompt_file: "C:/ProgramData/ziee/config/dev.yaml"` or `"\\\\host\\share\\x"` contains no `..` and does not start with `/`, yet `Path::join` on Windows DISCARDS the bundle root for both, so the escape is caught only by the bundle-present ESCAPE branch — i.e. not at all on the draft `/validate` and `/validate-def` surfaces, and not at all in `load_raw_prompt` (which has no shape check whatsoever). Pre-existing, but the block is in the diff and the fix is one predicate (`Path::new(p).is_absolute() || p.contains(':') || p.starts_with('\\\\')`).

`canon.is_file()` conflates 'not a regular file' with 'stat failed': `Path::is_file` swallows every io::Error and returns false. Any EACCES/EIO/ENFILE on the bundle path now emits a BLOCKING `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING` (severity Error, validate.rs:471), and because `spawn_run`/`resume_run` call `validate_for_install` on EVERY run, a transient FS error turns a healthy workflow into a hard 400 instead of a retryable read failure at the step. Use `canon.metadata()` and distinguish `Ok(m) if !m.is_file()` from `Err(_)`.

REJECTED: 'filtering the empty prompt_file (`prompt_file_ref`) lets an unchecked path reach the read'. Ruled out: `PromptSource::File(f)` is produced only when `prompt_file_ref(prompt_file)` is `Some(f)` (validate.rs:1090), and `check_prompt_files` selects its `pf` through the SAME `prompt_file_ref` (validate.rs:1146). The set of strings that reach `load_raw_prompt`'s join is therefore exactly the set the validator shape/escape-checks — the refactor closed a divergence rather than opening one. The only string newly skipped is `""`, which the old code resolved to `bundle_root.join("")` == the bundle dir and never rejected.

REJECTED: 'the new `else if !canon.is_file()` breaks the canonicalize/confinement ordering'. Ruled out: the new arm is chained AFTER `!canon.starts_with(&root_canon)` and evaluates the same fully-resolved `canon`, so no escaping path can reach it and no path that reaches it can be outside the root. It is strictly additive (a subset of previously-accepted inputs is now rejected); no previously-rejected path becomes accepted.

REJECTED: '`canon.is_file()` follows a symlink and re-opens symlink escape'. Ruled out: `canon` is the output of `resolved.canonicalize()`, which resolves every symlink component; there is nothing left to follow, and the ESCAPE test already ran on the identical value. The author's comment ('a symlink to a real file still passes') is accurate.

REJECTED: 'the diff newly skips the confinement half when the bundle root is absent (`bundle_present`)'. Ruled out by `git show HEAD~1:src-app/server/src/modules/workflow/validate.rs` — `let bundle_present = bundle_root.is_dir();` and the `if !bundle_present { continue; }` are byte-identical to the parent commit. The diff did not change WHEN the existence/confinement half is skipped; it only changed which strings reach it (empty ones no longer do) and added a check after it.

REJECTED: 'the falsifiability control injects CSS via `page.addStyleTag` and is a script-injection surface'. Ruled out: it runs only in Playwright against the backend-free local gallery (`/gallery.html`), the content is a constant literal, and nothing is persisted or served.

The tightened validator this diff ships is not applied uniformly across execution surfaces reachable with the SAME permission. `test_workflow` (dev.rs:1094) is gated by `RequirePermissions<(WorkflowsExecute,)>` + `user_can_access` — identical to `/run` — but parses `workflow.yaml` and dispatches without ever calling `validate_for_install`, whereas `spawn_run` (runner.rs:1248) and `resume_run` (runner.rs:1552) do. So the security-layer findings `WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE`/`WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_ESCAPE` (and the new not-a-file check) gate one execution path and not its sibling. This diff strengthened the validator without closing the surface that ignores it.

REJECTED: 'making `prompt_source` / `prompt_file_ref` / `PromptSource` `pub` widens reachable capability'. Ruled out: they are pure, side-effect-free functions over two `Option<String>`s; they hold no handle, no pool, no path capability, and the `workflow` module is not re-exported outside the crate in a way that grants anything. No extractor, route, permission constant, or `Audience` is touched anywhere in either diff.

REJECTED: 'the new `/validate-def` test exercises a weakened gate'. Ruled out: it authenticates with the same `workflow_user` bearer token as the pre-existing test in the file and hits the same route; no route registration, permission constant, or handler extractor is modified in the diff.

REJECTED: 'the `promptSuppliedByFile` tightening is an authorization gate change'. Ruled out: it only decides whether a form field is marked required and whether a helper note renders; every definition still goes through `validate_for_install` server-side on save (`update_user_workflow_definition`, dev.rs:564) and on every run.

`WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING` is now overloaded onto a SECOND, semantically different condition (the path exists inside the bundle but is not a regular file) with a new message string, and the code comment claims 'the builder's author-facing copy needs no new entry'. That is wrong in effect: `validationCopy.ts:104` maps this code to exactly one sentence — "This step points at a prompt file that isn't in the workflow — add the file, or type the prompt in directly." For `prompt_file: "prompts/adir"` the file IS in the workflow, and the remedy the author is given ('add the file') does not clear the finding, so the author is stuck on a blocking error with unactionable copy. Same for `workflow_mcp/tools.rs` and any client keyed on the code. Either emit a distinct code (e.g. WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_NOT_A_FILE) or make the copy fn discriminate.

`WORKFLOW_PROMPT_BOTH` silently STOPS firing for a wire shape it used to reject. Old rule: `has_file = prompt_file.is_some()`, so `{prompt: "hi", prompt_file: ""}` produced a blocking WORKFLOW_PROMPT_BOTH and a 400 from install / `PUT /definition`. New rule routes that through `prompt_file_ref`, which filters `""` to absent, so `prompt_source` returns `Inline("hi")` and NO finding is emitted at all — a previously-rejected definition now validates clean and runs. This loosening is undocumented in the doc comment (which only argues the empty-`prompt:` direction) and is UNCOVERED by the new tests: TEST-2 asserts `("","p.md")`, `("",None)`, `(None,"")`, `("","")`, `("   ","p.md")` and `("hi","p.md")`, but never `("hi","")`; TEST-1's matrix pairs `Some("hi")` with `Some("")` only through an implication assertion that both sides now satisfy, so it cannot see the change either.

The two new blocking findings are enforced on EVERY run, not just at install, so they retro-break already-installed workflows with no migration or back-compat path. `spawn_run` (runner.rs:1248) and `resume_run` (runner.rs:1552) both call `validate_for_install`, which returns the FIRST Error-severity finding as a 400. After this diff: (a) a workflow carrying `prompt_file: ""` now 400s at `POST /api/workflows/{id}/runs` with WORKFLOW_PROMPT_MISSING where it previously created a run and failed only that step; (b) a workflow whose `prompt_file:` names a directory now 400s with WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING; and worst, (c) an IN-FLIGHT durable run of either kind can no longer be resumed — `resume_run` hard-errors before `preflight`, so a `waiting`/`resumable` run is stranded rather than continuing. The status-code contract for `/runs` changes from 'run created, step-level failure' to 'request rejected'.

Runtime behaviour change not called out anywhere in the diff: `{prompt: "", prompt_file: absent}` used to match the old `(Some(p), None)` arm and return `Ok("")` — the step ran with an empty prompt. It now returns `Err("step '<id>' has invalid prompt config")`, surfaced to the client as a step failure `prompt render: step '<id>' has invalid prompt config`. Defensible, but it is a behaviour flip for any pre-existing (e.g. `is_dev`, or pre-check-era) workflow that relied on an empty prompt, and TEST-6 pins the new behaviour without a note that it is a change rather than a fix.

The client-side documentation of the client/server contract is now stale and actively misleading — it is the only place the rule is written down for the next reader. `LlmStepForm.tsx:19-36`, `LlmMapStepForm.tsx:22-24,66` and `stepForms.ts:193` still state "dispatch.rs's load_raw_prompt, which matches only (Some,None)/(None,Some), fails the RUN with 'invalid prompt config'" — the exact behaviour this diff removed — and `stepForms.ts:193` still says "WORKFLOW_PROMPT_MISSING fires only on `!has_prompt && !has_file`" using the old `has_file = is_some()` definition. Only the `promptSuppliedByFile` doc block was updated.

The kit change converts the addon variants from physical `pl/ml`/`pr/mr` to logical `ps/pe`, but the one in-kit CONSUMER that overrides them was not converted: `command.tsx:73` still forces `*:data-[slot=input-group-addon]:pl-2!`. Two consequences. (1) In LTR the `!important` physical `padding-left:0.5rem` now beats the new `has-[>button]:ps-1`, so a command-palette addon holding a button gets 8px instead of the intended 4px — the visual result the diff's comment computes ('within 0.8px of the old optical result') does not hold there. (2) In RTL, `pl-2!` sets `padding-left` while `ps-*` sets `padding-inline-start` (= `padding-right`), so BOTH apply and the addon gets asymmetric padding — a new RTL defect created by the half-migration. The new `input-group-overflow.spec.ts` cannot catch either: it only asserts the addon does not extend PAST the group.

(The guard checking only the CODE and not the message is precisely why the copy mismatch filed above slips through it.)

TEST-3's FIRST block is IDLE against this diff. `codes(prompt:"" + prompt_file:"prompts/real.md")` then asserts !BOTH && !MISSING && !FILE_MISSING — but the PRE-diff validator already returned exactly that (old code: `has_prompt = prompt.filter(!is_empty).is_some()` = false, `has_file = prompt_file.is_some()` = true → neither branch fires; real.md exists so no FILE_MISSING). Revert BOTH production hunks and this block still passes. The defect it is captioned for ('states that used to validate GREEN and then fail the run') lived entirely on the DISPATCH side, which this test never touches. Only the 2nd (empty prompt_file → MISSING) and 3rd (directory → FILE_MISSING) blocks of TEST-3 are load-bearing.

TEST-4 (`validate_def_prompt_source_verdicts`) is credited in its doc-comment with 'the TWO prompt states that used to validate GREEN and then fail the RUN', but only ONE of its three cases can go red. Case 1 (`prompt:""` + `prompt_file:"prompts/task.md"`, asserted !BOTH && !MISSING at :156) passes identically on the pre-diff validator — the old `has_prompt` filter already normalised an empty prompt to absent. Case 3 (:178) is self-declared a control. So one integration test is being credited with several distinct guarantees that rest on a single load-bearing assertion (case 2, `prompt_file:""` → MISSING). The whole endpoint-level test also cannot see the OTHER half of the fix (the directory verdict) because /validate-def passes a non-existent bundle root (handlers/dev.rs:952), which the doc acknowledges — meaning the endpoint the author actually reads still reports nothing for the directory case.

The falsifiability control does NOT mirror the reverted production selector. The removed CSS was `has-[>button]:mr-[-0.3rem]` / `has-[>kbd]:mr-[-0.15rem]` — i.e. the negative margin applied ONLY to an addon with a DIRECT `button`/`kbd` child. The control injects `[data-slot=input-group-addon][data-align=inline-end]{margin-inline-end:-0.3rem}` UNCONDITIONALLY, so it can go red via an addon that carries neither. Consequently a green control does not prove the probe would catch the real revert; it proves only that the probe reacts to *some* addon. It should inject `...[data-align="inline-end"]:has(>button){margin-inline-end:-0.3rem}` to be a faithful re-injection. It also injects only the -0.3rem button variant, never the -0.15rem kbd variant that was likewise removed.

The anti-vacuity guard is weaker than the property it protects. `groups.filter(g => g.addonPastEnd !== null).length > 0` only proves SOME inline-end addon was rendered; the defect class only exists for an addon with a direct `<button>`/`<kbd>` child. If the gallery ever renders comboboxes with `showTrigger={false} showClear={false}` (an empty addon — combobox.tsx:79-92 guards both children behind flags), both `toEqual([])` assertions plus this guard pass while measuring a configuration that could never have been broken. The absence-shaped assertions at :113 and :121 are exactly the shape that passes when the thing being measured stopped being found in its defective form.

A SILENT behaviour flip introduced by `prompt_source` is asserted nowhere. `prompt: "hi"` + `prompt_file: ""` used to be WORKFLOW_PROMPT_BOTH at validate (old `has_file = prompt_file.is_some()` is TRUE for `Some("")`) and an Err at dispatch; it now validates clean and RUNS the inline prompt. TEST-2 (validate.rs:1793) enumerates the normalisation table but omits exactly this pair — it asserts `(Some(""),Some(""))`, `(Some("   "),Some("p.md"))`, `(Some("hi"),Some("p.md"))`, never `(Some("hi"),Some(""))`. TEST-3's 'pre-existing verdicts unmoved' block omits it too. TEST-1 walks the cell but cannot detect the change: old and new AGREE there (old = reject/reject, new = accept/accept), so the iff holds either way. A user-visible verdict moved with zero coverage.

The `inline-start` variant is changed identically (`pl-2 has-[>button]:ml-[-0.3rem] has-[>kbd]:ml-[-0.15rem]` → `ps-2 has-[>button]:ps-1 has-[>kbd]:ps-1.5`) but NO assertion in the diff can see it. `probeGroups` (input-group-overflow.spec.ts:70) queries only `[data-align="inline-end"]`, and the other signal cannot substitute: in LTR, content overflowing to the LEADING edge is not reflected in `scrollWidth - clientWidth`, so a re-introduced negative `margin-inline-start` would leave both `scrolling` and `bleeding` empty. Half the changed production line is unguarded.

The test's headline claim is wider than what it checks: 'the client's file-backed predicate must mirror the backend's ONE prompt-source rule, `validate.rs::prompt_source`, EXACTLY.' Only the prompt_file half is mirrored. The prompt half DIVERGES and is left uncovered: client `promptField` (stepForms.ts:209) is `z.string().trim().min(1)`, so `prompt: "   "` is a client-side error, while `prompt_source` deliberately (DEC-3, pinned by TEST-2 at validate.rs:1817) classifies `"   "` as a valid `Inline`. The pre-existing test at stepForms.test.ts:279 actively asserts the client's divergent verdict. So the two sides do not in fact agree 'exactly', and nothing in the diff measures that seam.

`PROMPT_CODES` is a hand-maintained duplicate of the prompt slice of `validate.rs::KNOWN_CODES` (validate.rs:377-382). TEST-1's whole verdict is `findings.filter(|e| PROMPT_CODES.contains(&e.code))` — so any prompt-related finding code added later that is not manually copied into this array is silently EXCLUDED from the INV-1 iff, and the matrix goes on reporting green while no longer covering it. Derive the list from KNOWN_CODES (or a prefix match on `WORKFLOW_PROMPT`) instead of restating it.

Nothing asserts the SPACING outcome of the sdk change, only containment. The kit comment claims the new `ps-1`/`pe-1`/`ps-1.5`/`pe-1.5` padding lands 'within 0.8px of the old optical result'; the new spec would pass equally with `pe-8`, with the padding removed entirely, or with the button child deleted. The RTL branch of the probe (`addonPastEnd = rtl ? groupBox.left - a.left : ...`) is never executed. The new directory verdict reuses WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING, but the author-facing copy keyed off that code (ui/src/modules/workflow/components/builder/validationCopy.ts:104-105: "points at a prompt file that isn't in the workflow — add the file") misdescribes the directory case (the path IS in the workflow; it is a directory). `prompt_source`, `prompt_file_ref` and `PromptSource` are declared `pub` but every caller is in-crate (validate.rs:687/1146, dispatch.rs:120). `pub(crate)` matches the actual reach (compare `dispatch::resolve_prompt`, which IS `pub(crate)`); as written they widen the module's public surface with no consumer.

TEST-1 drives `load_raw_prompt` directly, not the two real entry points. `resolve_prompt` (dispatch.rs:86) additionally template-renders the loaded body, and `agent_dispatch.rs:1101` is the agent-kind caller — neither is exercised, so the `kind="agent"` and `kind="llm"` arms of the 60-cell matrix are literally the same code path as `llm_map` (the kind string only changes what the VALIDATOR sees). The matrix's per-kind dimension is 3× wider than the runner behaviour it actually varies.

REJECTED: `promptSuppliedByFile`'s new emptiness rule is on a real production path — three form callers (LlmStepForm.tsx:22, LlmMapStepForm.tsx:25, AgentStepForm.tsx:62) plus `configErrors` (stepForms.ts:306), which is what the builder renders. Not a test-only helper.

REJECTED: TEST-6 is NOT hollow. REJECTED: TEST-2 is not merely a tautology on the new function. REJECTED: `an EMPTY prompt_file leaves the prompt requirement in force` is load-bearing and its own non-vacuity control is real. Half-converted RTL: the addon variants (lines 47-50) were converted to logical padding (ps/pe), but their COMPANION rules on the InputGroup root are still physical - `has-[>[data-align=inline-end]]:[&>input]:pr-1.5` and `has-[>[data-align=inline-start]]:[&>input]:pl-1.5`. `data-align` is expressed in logical terms and `order-first`/`order-last` flip under RTL, so in RTL the input's clearance padding lands on the side AWAY from the addon. Measured live (dir=rtl, align=inline-start, addon visually on the right): computed input padding-left=6px / padding-right=0px - 6px of dead padding on the far edge and 0px where the addon actually is. Same for inline-end mirrored. This is exactly the inconsistency the change's own comment claims to fix ('ml/mr/pl/pr do not flip under RTL'), left half-done one line above. Fix: pl-1.5 -> ps-1.5, pr-1.5 -> pe-1.5.

NEW RTL regression: the gap between the input's text/caret edge and the addon's child collapses to 0px in EVERY RTL case. Measured (400px group, dir=rtl, old inline styles vs new classes) - inline-start AND inline-end both: button 3.2px -> 0px, kbd 5.61px -> 0px, plain icon/text 8.00px -> 0px. Cause: under RTL the old physical `pl-2`/`pr-2` accidentally landed on the addon's INNER side and supplied that separation; the new `ps-2`/`pe-2` correctly moves it to the OUTER side, and the inner separation that should replace it (the root's input pl-1.5/pr-1.5, finding line 17) is still physical and lands on the far side. Net RTL: the addon is no longer flush against the group border (measured child inset 0px -> 4/6/8px, a real fix) but the child now abuts the input content edge with zero clearance. LTR is unaffected (input->child gap measured at exactly 6.00px old and new, all three child shapes, both aligns).

The explanatory comment quotes the removed class verbatim (`has-[>button]:mr-[-0.3rem]`, plus `-0.3rem`/`-0.15rem`), and Tailwind v4's content scanner is a raw-text candidate extractor that does NOT skip comments - so the utilities the change deletes are still emitted. Verified in the LIVE bundle at :5397: `.has-\[\>button\]\:mr-\[-0\.3rem\]{margin-right:-0.3rem}`, `.has-\[\>button\]\:ml-\[-0\.3rem\]`, `.has-\[\>kbd\]\:mr-\[-0\.15rem\]` and `.has-\[\>kbd\]\:ml-\[-0\.15rem\]` are all still present, and a repo-wide grep shows the ONLY remaining occurrences of those strings are this comment plus two parent-spec docblocks. Consequence: dead off-grid CSS ships, and the exact footgun remains applicable by class name (a consumer `className="has-[>button]:mr-[-0.3rem]"` still reproduces the overflow with no CSS change). Rephrase the comment to break the candidate (e.g. 'a negative inline margin of -0.3rem' without the class syntax).

The addon's own click-to-focus hit area shrinks in the inline axis. InputGroupAddon carries an onClick that focuses the sibling input, so its padding gutter is an interactive surface; measured addon border-box width 32px -> 28px with a button child (-4px) and 23.2px -> 21.2px with a kbd child (-2px), unchanged (24px/22px/8px) for icon/text/empty. The controls themselves are untouched (button measured 24x24 in every old/new x LTR/RTL x align combination, so WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 is unaffected) and part of the lost 4px previously sat OUTSIDE the group's border, so this is minor - but it is a real reduction of the 'click the gutter to focus' strip and worth a conscious accept.

Containment is fixed only in the inline axis; the addon still overflows its group VERTICALLY and the change leaves it. Measured on all 9 live gallery input-groups at 390/768/1400px: group height 32px (h-8, 30px content box after the 1px borders) vs addon height 36px -> 4px of overflow (2px top + 2px bottom), from `py-1.5` (12px) + a 24px `icon-xs` button. Cosmetically invisible today (the addon is transparent and the button stays optically centred) and it cannot scroll (group overflow-x/y computed `visible`), but it breaks the same 'the addon sits inside its group' invariant this change asserts, and the new spec only probes the inline axis so it would never go red. `py-1` or `h-full` on the addon would close it.

The inline-start half of the fix is real but unguarded. Measured old vs new for align=inline-start with a button child: the addon's border box used to start 4.8px before the group's inner content edge, i.e. 3.8px past the 1px border (overhang 4.80 -> 0.00 after the change; kbd 2.39 -> 0.00). That start-side bleed produces NO `scrollWidth` growth in LTR (browsers do not make start-side overflow scrollable), which is why it was never noticed - and the new Layer-A spec only queries `[data-align="inline-end"]` and never toggles the gallery's DIRECTION control, so a future regression of the `inline-start` variant (or of either variant under RTL) is invisible to it. Widen the probe to both aligns.

REJECTED: off-grid / arbitrary values introduced. `ps-2`/`pe-2` = 8px, `ps-1`/`pe-1` = 4px, `ps-1.5`/`pe-1.5` = 6px - all on the Tailwind scale, with 6px being the 2px half-step the kit already uses elsewhere in this same file (`py-1.5`, `px-2.5`). The change strictly IMPROVES grid conformance: it removes the only two genuinely arbitrary values in the variants (`-0.3rem` = 4.8px, `-0.15rem` = 2.4px). No color token, radius, or arbitrary value is introduced by the diff.

REJECTED: `has-[>button]:pe-1` fails to override the base `pe-2`, leaving 8px and shifting the button 4px inward. Verified it wins: `:has(> button)` adds a type-selector's worth of specificity (0,1,1 vs 0,1,0), and all 9 live gallery addons compute `padding-inline-end: 4px` with `padding-inline-start: 0px`. Both `.has-\[\>button\]\:ps-1` and `.has-\[\>kbd\]\:ps-1\.5` are present in the shipped bundle even though no in-repo addon has a kbd child.

REJECTED: an addon containing BOTH a button and a kbd resolves ambiguously / differently than before. `has-[>button]:pe-1` and `has-[>kbd]:pe-1.5` have IDENTICAL specificity (0,1,1) so the winner is Tailwind's emitted source order - measured 6px (kbd wins). That is exactly the old behaviour, which had the same same-property tie between `ml-[-0.3rem]` and `ml-[-0.15rem]` (measured old net inset 5.61px vs new 6.00px, delta +0.39px). Not a regression. Worth knowing that in the `inline-start`+both case the padding the rule is meant to tighten against the BUTTON (first child) is the kbd's 6px, not 4px - but again, unchanged from before.

REJECTED: perceptible LTR visual shift. Measured child inset from the group's inner content edge, old -> new: button 3.20px -> 4.00px (+0.80), kbd 5.61px -> 6.00px (+0.39), plain icon 8.00px -> 8.00px (0.00), text 8.00 -> 8.00 (0.00), empty addon 8px padding unchanged. The input->child gap is byte-identical at 6.00px in all six LTR combinations, and the input merely gains 0.8px of width where the addon stopped hanging out. Sub-pixel-class; the commit's '<=0.8px' claim is accurate.

REJECTED: focus ring clipped or tap target reduced on the control. The button measures 24x24 CSS px in every old/new x LTR/RTL x align x child-shape combination (WCAG 2.2 SC 2.5.8 minimum met, unchanged). The group computes `overflow-x: visible` so nothing clips the ring, and the button now sits 4.00px from the group's inner edge instead of 3.20px, so ring clearance marginally IMPROVES. No aria/role/label surface is touched by the diff.

REJECTED: tailwind-merge override fragility - a consumer passing `className="px-2"` to InputGroupAddon would have tw-merge drop the base `ps-2` but NOT the differently-modified `has-[>button]:ps-1`, leaving an asymmetric 4px/8px result that the old margin-based code could not produce. Real but purely theoretical here: the two in-repo consumers (combobox.tsx:79 ComboboxInput, command.tsx:82 CommandInput) pass no className at all to the addon, and a repo-wide grep finds no third consumer of InputGroupAddon.

TEST-1 claims to walk "the whole authorable state space" (doc at :1949) but the `files` array deliberately contains only shape-SAFE paths (None, "", prompts/real.md, prompts/adir, prompts/nope.md). The one state class where validate and dispatch STILL disagree is excluded: `prompt_file: "prompts/../prompts/real.md"` makes the validator emit WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE (validate.rs:1152, textual `contains("..")`) — which IS in PROMPT_CODES (:1903) — while `load_raw_prompt` (:120-127) does `bundle_root.join(rel)` with no `..`/absolute/confinement check and returns Ok. Add that one cell and the INV-1 assertion at :1988 goes red. So the invariant the whole change is built around is asserted only over the subset where it happens to hold; the matrix's shape gives false confidence that it is total.

The doc-comment claims more than the code supports: "a definition the validator reports green cannot fail here, and one it reports red cannot quietly succeed here." Only the XOR/emptiness half is shared. The validator's other prompt verdicts — WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE, _ESCAPE, _FILE_MISSING — have no counterpart in `load_raw_prompt`, which joins the raw `rel` onto `bundle_root` and reads it (:123-126). A red-at-validate `../..` path would quietly succeed here if it ever reached the runner (today only install-time validation stops it — a fact the comment does not mention). Scope the claim to the XOR, or state that path safety is enforced only at install.

The SAME rule is now implemented independently in Rust (`validate.rs::prompt_source`, the non-empty filter) and TypeScript (`promptSuppliedByFile`, `typeof pf === 'string' && pf.length > 0`), and NOTHING catches them drifting. Both new tests are self-referential: validate.rs:1794 pins the Rust side, stepForms.test.ts:394 pins the TS side against a prose description of the Rust side. A deliberate Rust change (e.g. adopting trim(), which TEST-2's own comment anticipates) updates the Rust test and leaves the TS predicate silently stale. This is doubly avoidable because the module ALREADY has a cross-language drift guard of exactly the right shape: validationCopy.ts:19-23 documents a Rust test (`validation_codes_are_registered_and_humanised`) that READS the TS file and fails the backend suite on drift. The new rule did not get one.

The Rust/TS divergence is not hypothetical — a divergent cell is actively pinned. `{ prompt: '   ', prompt_file: 'prompts/task.md' }` is asserted to produce NO client-side prompt error, while the new backend rule reads it as `PromptSource::Both` → WORKFLOW_PROMPT_BOTH (validate.rs:1091, pinned at validate.rs:1818). Client-side `promptField` also rejects a whitespace-only prompt with no file (z.string().trim().min(1), stepForms.ts:209-210) where the backend accepts it as `Inline("   ")`. The backend panel is a backstop for the first case, so impact is limited to a per-field error that never appears — but a test now certifies the disagreement rather than the agreement.

Stale comment describing code that no longer exists. `promptField`'s doc says it MIRRORS "validate.rs (~681-691), the sole authority" and then transcribes the PRE-FIX rule verbatim: `has_file = prompt_file.is_some()`. That is precisely the line this diff deleted (validate.rs now routes through `prompt_source`, where an empty string is absent). The diff updated the sibling comment 23 lines below but not this one, so the file now states the rule two different ways. The `~681-691` line reference is also stale (the code is at 676-702).

Comment makes a claim the code does not support: "`''`/`'   '`/`null` all pass, matching the backend's reading of 'no typed prompt'". Under the rule this very diff introduces, `'   '` is NOT "no typed prompt" to the backend — `prompt_source` returns `Inline("   ")` (validate.rs:1089), and the diff's own TS test at stepForms.test.ts:400-403 says so explicitly ("the backend filters on is_empty(), NOT trim()"). The comment and the test in the same change contradict each other.

The (newly expanded) doc-comment for `promptSuppliedByFile` is orphaned: it is immediately followed by a second JSDoc block (:223-230) documenting `PROMPT_FROM_FILE_NOTE` (:231). Tooling attaches the second block to the const and the first to nothing, so the exported function at :236 has NO hover doc — the ten lines of rationale the diff just wrote are invisible at the only place a caller would look. Move the block down to sit directly above `export function promptSuppliedByFile`.

The change unified the RULE but not the ACCESSOR. Extracting the `(prompt, prompt_file)` pair is still an open, hand-written `if let`/`match` over `{Llm, LlmMap, Agent}` in at least six places — validate.rs:676 (XOR check), validate.rs:1143 (check_prompt_files), dispatch.rs:146, dispatch.rs:300, agent_dispatch.rs:1075, dispatch.rs:1931 (test helper) — plus buildStepZodSchema's switch (stepForms.ts:260-278). Every one of them fails SILENTLY for a new kind: the `if let` simply doesn't match (no XOR verdict at all), `check_prompt_files` falls to `_ => None` (no file check), and the test helper falls to `_ => (None, None)`. There is already an exhaustive `impl StepConfig` with `kind_str()` at validate.rs:254-265 — a `pub fn prompt_fields(&self) -> Option<(&Option<String>, &Option<String>)>` there would make the compiler flag every new kind exactly once.

The INV-1 matrix hardcodes `for kind in ["llm", "llm_map", "agent"]`, and its driver `prompt_fields` (:1931) returns `(None, None)` for anything else. A seventh StepConfig variant carrying the same field pair is therefore silently outside the invariant the test exists to protect — it neither fails nor covers. Deriving the kind list from `StepConfig` (or asserting the list's length against the variant count) would make the omission loud.

A SHARED SDK component was fixed, but its only regression guard lives in the CONSUMER app (src-app/ui/tests/e2e/visual/input-group-overflow.spec.ts). The sdk diff is the .tsx and nothing else — no test, no story, no assertion inside sdk/packages/kit. Any other consumer of @ziee/kit gets the fix with no guard, and an SDK-side edit that reintroduces the negative margin passes every check that ships with the SDK. For a shared framework the property test belongs beside the component (or at minimum the SDK needs a pointer to the consumer-side guard).

Shared SDK source now cites a consumer-private artifact: "(`.lifecycle/workflow-builder-ux/FIX_ROUND-2.md`)". That path exists only in the ziee app repo, not in the SDK, so an SDK reader (or any other consuming app) hits a dangling reference in the one comment explaining why the variant is written this way. Inline the reason (it largely is) and drop the app-branch path, or move the narrative to the consumer-side spec that can resolve it.

The change's stated rationale — "`ml`/`mr`/`pl`/`pr` do not flip under RTL although `data-align` is expressed in logical terms" (:30) — is applied to the addon variants but NOT to the identical defect ten lines above in the same file: the InputGroup root still carries `has-[>[data-align=inline-end]]:[&>input]:pr-1.5` and `has-[>[data-align=inline-start]]:[&>input]:pl-1.5`, i.e. physical padding keyed off a logical alignment. Under RTL the input's inner gap lands on the wrong side. The new probe cannot catch it either (see the RTL note on the spec).

`prompt_source(prompt: &Option<String>, prompt_file: &Option<String>)` takes two adjacent parameters of the SAME type whose meanings are opposite; swapping them compiles and silently inverts the rule (a file path becomes the inline prompt and vice versa). The same hazard is inherited by `load_raw_prompt(step_id, bundle_root, prompt, prompt_file)` (dispatch.rs:113-118) and by every call site that must keep them in order. A single `&StepConfig` (via the accessor suggested above) or a two-field struct would make the swap unrepresentable — worth it for a function whose entire purpose is making a class of mistake impossible.

`PromptSource::Missing | PromptSource::Both` collapse into one message, "step '{id}' has invalid prompt config". The new enum has just made the distinction available at zero cost, and the two faults have OPPOSITE fixes (add wording vs remove one of the two sources) — the validator says so in two distinct codes. The runtime error should tell the operator which one it is; as written it is the least actionable string the function can produce.

The new directory case reuses WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING and the comment presents that as cost-free ("Reuses the existing code, so the builder's author-facing copy needs no new entry"). But the author-facing copy keyed to that code is "This step points at a prompt file that isn't in the workflow — add the file, or type the prompt in directly" (validationCopy.ts:104-105) — which misdescribes the fault: the path IS in the workflow, it is a directory. The backend message ("is not a file in the bundle") never reaches the author because the humanisation is keyed on code only. Reuse avoided a drift-guard failure at the price of a wrong sentence to the person who has to fix it.

`prompt_file_ref` is `pub` but has no consumer outside validate.rs (only :1087 and :1146). Beyond the unnecessary public surface, it is a misuse magnet: it exposes HALF the shared rule, so an outside caller can ask "is there a file?" and silently miss the Both/Missing arms the abstraction exists to force them through. Make it private (or fold it into the accessor) and keep `prompt_source` the only public door.

`PromptSource` + `prompt_source` are placed at :1049-1105, wedged between `collect_template_strings` and `check_prompt_files` — i.e. among the private check helpers, ~800 lines away from the `StepConfig` definition (:150) and `impl StepConfig` (:254) they describe, in a module whose NAME says validation even though the rule is definition semantics that a runtime module now imports. A reader of dispatch.rs following the import lands in the middle of the validator's internals. Placing it next to `impl StepConfig` (or in types.rs) would make the shared-vocabulary intent legible without changing any dependency edge.

`assert_eq!(checked, 60, ...)` hardcodes 3 kinds x 4 prompts x 5 files. It is meant as an anti-vacuity guard but it is a magic number that must be hand-recomputed whenever a case is added — and its failure mode reads as "the matrix must actually have been walked" rather than "you added a case, update the count". `kinds.len() * prompts.len() * files.len()` says the same thing and never goes stale.

The spec imports STANDALONE_PATH from './_gallery' but then hand-rolls the gallery-open sequence (goto + waitFor gallery-root + `waitForTimeout(1500)`, repeated at :142-146, plus a bare `waitForTimeout(200)` at :152) instead of calling the exported `openGallery()` in that same file, which waits on a POSITIVE signal (--primary applied, dir applied, document.fonts.ready). Duplicated setup with strictly weaker settling: the sleeps are undocumented magic numbers and are the usual source of flake in this suite.

The RTL branch (`addonPastEnd = rtl ? groupBox.left - a.left : ...`) is never exercised — VIEWPORTS (:34) only navigates LTR, and `_gallery.ts` exposes a `dir` parameter the spec ignores. The doc at :64-69 nonetheless claims the assertion "is RTL-correct". Untested branch backing a stated guarantee; adding one rtl case would also cover the physical pl/pr left on the InputGroup root.

The comment's numbers don't reconcile with each other or with the sibling comments: `-0.3rem` is 4.8px, but this text says the addon sat "3.8px outside its own group" and caused "5px of horizontal scrollable overflow", while builder-responsive.spec.ts:70-80 says ~4px and the new spec's header says 3.8px. They are presumably reconcilable via the group's 1px border (content box vs border box), but the comment switches reference boxes mid-sentence ("ends |margin| PAST the group's content box: ... 3.8px outside its own group") without saying so, so a future reader cannot check the arithmetic.

REJECTED: candidate — `ps-2` and `has-[>button]:ps-1` now set the SAME property on the same element, so the outcome would depend on Tailwind's emission order (whereas the old `pl-2` + `ml-[-0.3rem]` pair touched different properties). Ruled out: the `has-[>button]:` variant compiles to `&:has(>button)`, and `:has()` takes the specificity of its argument, so the variant selector is strictly more specific than the bare utility and wins regardless of order. twMerge also treats differently-modified utilities as non-conflicting, so both survive `cn()`. Deterministic as written.

REJECTED: candidate — the "within 0.8px of the old optical result" claim is unverifiable/wrong. Ruled out: it checks. Button, inline-start: old = pl-2 (8px) + ml -0.3rem (-4.8px) => child edge at +3.2px; new = ps-1 => +4px; delta 0.8px. kbd: old 8 - 2.4 = 5.6px; new ps-1.5 = 6px; delta 0.4px. The claim is accurate and the new values are on the 4px scale.

REJECTED: candidate — a runtime/dispatch module now depends on a validation module (`use ...validate::{PromptSource, prompt_source}`), the wrong direction. Ruled out: dispatch.rs already imported StepDef/StepConfig/OnError/OutputFormat from validate.rs before this change — validate.rs is the module that OWNS the definition types, so no new edge is created and no cycle is introduced. REJECTED: candidate — replacing `(&StepDef, &RunContext)` with `(&str, &Path)` widens the caller's burden. REJECTED: candidate — treating `prompt: "   "` as a real prompt while treating `""` as absent is an inconsistent normalisation. REJECTED: candidate — the new `!canon.is_file()` rejection could break existing workflows whose prompt_file names something non-regular. ITEM-4's readability upgrade stops one step short of the question its own comment asks ("it asks whether the path can be READ"): the new guard is `!canon.is_file()`, so a prompt_file naming a REAL but non-UTF8 file (a .png/.pdf shipped in the bundle) validates GREEN at install AND at the runner's pre-dispatch re-validate, then fails the RUN in load_raw_prompt with `read prompt_file 'x': stream did not contain valid UTF-8`. That is exactly DESIGN §1's non-negotiable ('a definition the validator reports GREEN must not fail at run for a prompt-configuration reason') and exactly the shape of the design's row-4 directory cell, just a different unreadable-ness. TEST-1's bundle contains no non-UTF8 file so the matrix cannot see it.

Asymmetry the shared rule introduces: `prompt: ""` is now refused because an empty prompt is degenerate (PromptSource::Missing -> Err), but `prompt_file:` pointing at a ZERO-BYTE file yields PromptSource::File -> Ok("") -> resolve_prompt -> `ChatMessage::user("")` at dispatch.rs:176 with NO emptiness guard, while the validator is GREEN. DESIGN §1's second half ('a definition the validator reports RED must not quietly succeed at run with a degenerate prompt') is upheld for the inline half and left open for the file half — the same degenerate empty LLM call the inline fix exists to prevent. TEST-1's bundle has only a non-empty real.md, so the matrix has no empty-file row.

The named acceptance test asserts only AGREEMENT (`prompt_findings.is_empty() == run.is_ok()`), never the DIRECTION DESIGN §1 chose. Mutation tried: drop the emptiness filter on the inline half of prompt_source (`let inline = prompt.as_deref();`, validate.rs:1086) — i.e. adopt dispatch's old rule instead of validate's. Then ('',file) is Both/Err (agree) and ('',None) is Inline("")/Ok("") (agree): all 60 cells still pass, yet DESIGN's 'Direction' section explicitly forbids that resolution (it re-creates the false red on the state the builder's own remedy produces) and row 2 requires that state to be RED. NOT caught by TEST-1; caught only by TEST-2/TEST-3 (validate.rs:1794/1794+), which are not the stated acceptance proof.

TEST-1 claims 'the whole authorable state space' and its PROMPT_CODES list includes WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE and WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_ESCAPE, but the `files` array carries no '..'/absolute/escaping path — precisely the rows where the asserted implication FAILS today. check_prompt_files pushes UNSAFE and `continue`s (validate.rs:1150-1157) while load_raw_prompt still does a raw `bundle_root.join(rel)` with no path-safety check, so `prompt_file: prompts/../prompts/real.md` is validator-RED and run-OK. Adding that one string to `files` turns TEST-1 red. The shared rule therefore does NOT unify path-safety, only presence/emptiness; the claim of exhaustiveness is overstated.

ITEM-7's permanent guard is not reached by the enforced gate. `npm run gate:ui` (the repo's stated UI exit condition per CLAUDE.md) runs the visual layer with an explicit allow-list, `CFG.visualSpecs` = [layout, form-label-starvation, states, overlays, chat-collapse-borders] (sdk/packages/gallery/scripts/gate-ui.mjs:184-186). `input-group-overflow.spec.ts` was not added, although the sibling the PLAN says it mirrors (form-label-starvation.spec.ts) IS listed. The one CI job that runs the whole visual config unfiltered is path-gated on `src-app/ui/**` / package.json / the workflow file. The guarded component lives in the `sdk` submodule, so the change class that both CAUSED this defect and DELIVERED its fix — an sdk submodule-pointer bump touching only the `sdk` gitlink — does not trigger visual-tests.yml. Combined with the gate:ui allow-list omission, a future kit regression in inputGroupAddonVariants can land with neither guard executing.

Scope beyond DESIGN §3 as written. §2 names only the `inline-end` addon ('inputGroupAddonVariants' inline-end variant is order-last pr-2 has-[>button]:mr-[-0.3rem]…') and §3 says 'Any other kit spacing … out of scope. This branch fixes the two recorded residuals and nothing else.'
